facts: Deterministic 32-bit hash (FNV-1a). Same campaign, same day, same cap, a jitter that moved between two reads inside one day would let a caller reroll the ceiling by retrying.

Linear from `startCents` to `targetCents`, with jitter applied only WHILE descending: the taper wobbles, the floor does not. An advertiser told "it settles around 300 a day" should get 300, not 270 on an unlucky Tuesday six weeks later.

ai.title: BudgetGlide deterministic daily cap taper
ai.summary: Added `BudgetGlide` interface and `glidedDailyBudgetCents` function to `common/src/constants/freebuff-ads.ts`. This implements a linear daily budget taper with deterministic jitter, using an FNV-1a hash of campaign seed and date to prevent predictable cap changes. `effectiveDailyBudgetCents` gates the taper, applying it only to non-subscription campaigns to avoid altering billed prices.

eli5.text: Campaigns that were set to lower their daily ad delivery over time now do it smoothly on a schedule instead of dropping off a cliff. If you run a campaign that is not billed by subscription, the system can be told to start at a higher daily cap and gradually ease it down to a target amount over a set number of days, with a small amount of built-in randomness so the cap landing on any given day can't be predicted from a calendar. Each day gets one fixed number for that campaign, chosen with a hash so it stays the same whether you check in the morning or evening. If your campaign is paid through a subscription, the schedule is ignored entirely and you keep seeing the same daily budget you are charged for.

ai.title: Ignore .claude/worktrees to prevent nested git worktrees and duplicate
ai.summary: Added .claude/worktrees/ to .gitignore to exclude linked git worktrees created by agent tooling. Each worktree is a full checkout with its own .git file and generated migrations, so committing one nests a second working tree inside the repo and drags a duplicate migration index into whichever branch swept it up. Change scoped to .gitignore only; no code or config surfaces affected. Follow-up constraint: agent tooling must keep worktree directories under .claude/worktrees/ to remain excluded.

eli5.text: If you manage a software project, you know that sometimes extra folders get created when different parts of the system want to work independently, in this case, the tool the assistant uses to explore code can make its own full copy of the project to avoid messing up the main one. To keep those temporary copies from accidentally being saved into the project history (which would create confusing duplicates of important migration records), a small instruction was added to tell the project to ignore a specific folder where those copies live. If you look at the project settings file that controls what gets ignored, you will see a new entry pointing to that folder, ensuring only the main project stays clean and tracked.

entries.title: New slash command /reasoning
entries.summary: New slash commands: `/reasoning`. New files: `cli/src/commands/reasoning.ts`.

ai.title: /reasoning command sets per-model thinking effort in Freebuff
ai.summary: /reasoning [level] is a new Freebuff-only slash command that reads or sets how hard the selected model thinks, validated against the model's local ladder and persisted per model in settings.json as freebuffReasoningEfforts. It is freebuff-only because the ladder it reads is the FREEBUFF catalog's, and the metadata it sets is honored only for free-mode traffic (isFreebuffOriginatedRequest); on Codebuff the command takes a value and silently drops it. On send, cli/src/hooks/use-send-message.ts attaches the override as freebuff_reasoning_effort on extraCodebuffMetadata so it lands on the next message without restarting the session, while cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx memoizes picker width on reasoningEffortByModel and marks user-chosen rungs with a '*' suffix. Three supporting changes carry it: the store, the settings persistence, and the command/slash-command registration. The server re-clamps whatever the client sends against the model that actually runs the turn, so the effort is a request and not a final command.
ai.evidence: New file cli/src/commands/reasoning.ts exports handleReasoningCommand, added behind a freebuff-only command registration in cli/src/commands/command-registry.ts and cli/src/data/slash-commands.ts; cli/src/hooks/use-send-message.ts now reads getSelectedFreebuffReasoningEffort() and attaches it as freebuff_reasoning_effort on extraCodebuffMetadata; cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx memoizes row width on reasoningEffortByModel and renders a '*' suffix for user-chosen rungs; cli/src/state/freebuff-model-store.ts adds reasoningEffortByModel state plus getFreebuffReasoningEffortForModel/getEffectiveFreebuffReasoningEffort/getSelectedFreebuffReasoningEffort; cli/src/utils/settings.ts adds freebuffReasoningEfforts persistence and validates it against each model's ladder on load.
ai.migration: If you use the Freebuff CLI, you can run `/reasoning [low|high|max]` to override the thinking effort for your current model, or `/reasoning default` to return to the model's catalog default; overrides are stored per model, so switching models does not carry a rung across.
ai.unknowns: The consumer on the server side that resolves freebuff_reasoning_effort against the running model is not visible in this diff, and the rollout scope beyond the Freebuff CLI is not shown.

changes.what: New handleReasoningCommand(args) reads or sets the thinking effort for the selected Freebuff model, validating against the model's ladder and offering clear words ('default', 'auto', 'reset', 'clear', 'none') to drop the override.

The /reasoning command (aliases /effort, /think) is registered as freebuff-only, excluded from Codebuff via the FREEBUFF_ONLY_COMMANDS and FREEBUFF_ONLY_COMMAND_IDS gates, and wired to post its message into chat history.

Each Freebuff send now reads getSelectedFreebuffReasoningEffort() and, when non-null, attaches freebuff_reasoning_effort to extraCodebuffMetadata so the override reaches the requests layer for the next message.

The picker subscribes to reasoningEffortByModel so row-width memoization stays current, and renders a '· Reasoning: <rung>*' suffix where the '*' marks a rung the user chose, falling back to the catalog reasoningEffort otherwise.

Added reasoningEffortByModel state, setReasoningEffort (persisting per model), and the getFreebuffReasoningEffortForModel, getEffectiveFreebuffReasoningEffort, and getSelectedFreebuffReasoningEffort helpers, re-checking saves against the current ladder on every read.

Added freebuffReasoningEfforts to the Settings schema, loadFreebuffReasoningEfforts/saveFreebuffReasoningEffort accessors, and validation on load that drops any stored rung not offered by the model's current ladder.
